failure_analysis.hypothesis: The reconstructed SNR selector omitted a four-field completeness condition. Intersecting the full 741786 reconstructed candidates with positive Table 2 gmag, rmag, Per-g and Per-r values yields exactly the 730184 published Table 4 members. This is a strong empirical explanation, but the published text describes SNR selection and does not explicitly state the four-field gate.

findings: The r-band Zenodo archive MD5 and member CRC match; Info-ZIP produced a full stream with 109,971,576 rows and zero malformed rows.
The r archive member central-directory 32-bit size value equals the streamed size modulo 2^32; this is a size-field representation issue, not evidence of a truncated stream.
The CDS ReadMe reports 89,697,393 r rows, while the sum of Table 2 Nr is 109,970,858 and the Zenodo r stream has 109,971,576 rows.
Seq 615172 is a strong cross-band identity lead for Table 2 Seq 615170, but no automatic SourceID remapping is accepted.
The 718-row archive-versus-Table2 Nr residual and the full per-Seq mismatch distribution remain open.
A second independent r archive scan reproduced the first scan's archive and extracted-member hashes, byte count, CRC, row count and target/orphan summaries.
Full-dataset set intersection: SNR candidates ∩ positive gmag/rmag/Per-g/Per-r = exactly the 730184 published Table 4 members.

All 11602 candidate-only IDs fail at least one of the four Table 2 completeness fields; 11580 fail both field pairs, 17 have incomplete per-band periods only, and 5 have incomplete mean magnitudes only.
The 55 four-field-positive noncandidate controls fail at least one raw SNR threshold; 0 pass both bands.

The four-field completeness gate is the strongest current root-cause candidate, but is not explicitly stated in the published selection description; do not change the selector until the 17 cases and author methodology are resolved.
